criteria.text: Breakthrough cancer pain only (approval criterion 2 and denial criterion 1).
Patient is at least 18 years old (approval criterion 1).
Receiving around-the-clock opioid therapy for underlying persistent cancer pain (approval criterion 3; denial criterion 2).

Opioid tolerant: taking around-the-clock oral morphine ≥60 mg/day, transdermal fentanyl ≥25 mcg/hour, oxycodone ≥30 mg/day, oral hydromorphone ≥8 mg/day, or an equianalgesic dose of another opioid daily for at least 1 week. Approval criterion 4; denial criterion 3.

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Fentora (fentanyl buccal tablet). Strengths: 100, 200, 300, 400, 600 and 800 mcg.
Source Version 1, Last Updated 03/04/2010, Approved 3/19/2010. Retain stub effective_date 2016-10-03; the PDF does not state that as its effective date.
All four approval criteria and all three denial criteria are represented by the required predicates. Cancer pain is restricted to breakthrough cancer pain.

Opioid tolerant: taking around-the-clock oral morphine ≥60 mg/day, transdermal fentanyl ≥25 mcg/hour, oxycodone ≥30 mg/day, oral hydromorphone ≥8 mg/day, or an equianalgesic dose of another opioid daily for at least 1 week. Encoded as an attestation; dose equivalence and duration documentation require manual review.
Authorization: up to 6 months. Dispensing: 30-day supply. Quantity: 90 tablets per 30 days. These limits remain notes only and require manual review.

REMS/safety: review applicable TIRF REMS and fentanyl safety requirements manually. This archived PDF does not specify a REMS eligibility criterion; no REMS predicate is added. Breakthrough cancer pain, around-the-clock opioid therapy and opioid tolerance are required.
Remaining gaps: authorization duration, dispensing and quantity enforcement, documentation verification and REMS/safety review. Rules engine is the sole eligibility evaluator.
